messages:
Asha Patel: FYI — got a DSAR (ID: DSAR-2025-0423) requesting deletion of all personal data and derived embeddings. Customer region: EU. Data spans eu-west-1 primary + nightly backup snapshots in us-east-1. Need to plan deletion window, RBAC, and KMS access. Can we create a short-lived service account to perform cross-region delete and ensure auditability? cc @Tom @Lenora :eyes:
Tom Reynolds: Please drop the DSAR link and the exact dataset prefixes. We need the KMS key ARNs for any encrypted snapshots and the snapshot IDs. Also: remember backups in us-east might be immutable snapshots — check retention/hold.
Asha Patel: DSAR tracker: https://internal.redwood/priv/DSAR-2025-0423
Datasets: s3://redwood-embeddings/eu/tenant-42/*, es index tenant42-docs-*, pgdump snapshots: rdb/tenant42/2025-03-28/*.
KMS keys: arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111122223333:key/abcd-1111, arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/efgh-2222
Also one vector-db snapshot id: vecsnap-20250328-99.
Lenora Kim: Quick checks: legal_holds service shows no active hold for tenant-42 but we'll need Legal sign-off for cross-region erasure. If Legal flags it, we must stop. For audit: recommend the deletion runs under a distinct principal like `dsar-eraser@redwood` and include `dsar_id` in the KMS encryptionContext and CloudTrail event. That makes reconstruction straightforward.
Ravi Kumar: KMS note: granting `kms:Decrypt` cross-region/key-wide to an existing SA is risky. Suggest flow: 1) create ephemeral SA role `dsar-eraser-<ts>` in eu-west with narrowly scoped permissions (s3:DeleteObject for prefixes, es:Delete for specific indices, rds:DeleteSnapshot limited), 2) grant that role access to eu key only; 3) for us-east snapshots, either request owner to re-encrypt with an ephemeral us-east key we control OR ask SRE to perform a keyed delete under a cross-account, auditable process.
Ravi Kumar: Example least-priv policy (short):
```json
{
  "Statement": [
    {"Effect":"Allow","Action":["s3:DeleteObject"],"Resource":["arn:aws:s3:::redwood-embeddings/eu/tenant-42/*"]},
    {"Effect":"Allow","Action":["es:ESHttpDelete"],"Resource":["arn:aws:es:eu-west-1:111122223333:domain/tenant42*/*"]}
  ]
}
```
Tom Reynolds: Also remember the vuln triage note from last month — we had an incident where a broad `s3:DeleteObject` was accidentally applied to a parent prefix. For this PR, please ensure the policy uses exact prefixes (no wildcards that include other tenants). I'll raise an SRE runbook step: verify a dry-run with `aws s3 ls --recursive --summarize` and `es:simulate` before actual deletion.
Asha Patel: Good call. I'll draft a short-lived role PR and include explicit resource ARNs. Plan: create role, run pre-delete simulations (list-only), then run delete with `--audit-context dsar=DSAR-2025-0423` header, and push CloudTrail events to our immutable audit bucket.
Lenora Kim: Legal: @Legal Bot — please review DSAR-2025-0423 for cross-region deletion approval. We need explicit sign-off before any us-east snapshot handling.
Legal Bot: Auto-note: request received. Legal will triage within 24 working hours. If this is urgent, escalate via legal-escalations@redwood.com.
Tom Reynolds: Ops reminder: add a CloudTrail event selector that includes `DeleteObject`/`DeleteSnapshot` and ensure the trail is writing to `s3://redwood-audit/immutable/` with SSE-KMS using audit key (arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111122223333:key/audit-3333).
Ravi Kumar: One more KMS tip — use an encryptionContext like { "dsar_id":"DSAR-2025-0423", "tenant":"tenant-42" } and log it. That way if a key policy is misused, you can filter CloudTrail by encryptionContext fields.
Asha Patel: Noted. I'll include encryptionContext on any re-encrypt/delete operations. I'll also attach the vulnerability triage ticket: VULN-2025-0178 (service acct permission audit) to the PR so reviewers pay attention.
Tom Reynolds: Sounds good. I can review the role + runbook this afternoon. If Legal signs off, we can schedule the delete for 16:00 UTC tomorrow.
Asha Patel: Thanks all — I'll open the PR now and ping for reviews. :thumbsup:
